To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“The deployment of a reconfigurable intelligent switchable surface in the vicinity of the BS-array can control the eigenspace structure of the massive MIMO channel in an intentional manner.”
(1) the RIS can be used to control the channel’s eigenspaces, and (2) the eigenspaces of the channel are controlled by the switching state of the RIS.
the proposed RIS structure can be deployed to control the eigenspace structure of the uplink channel between a massive MIMO array and a cluster of UEs.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing a new paradigm for wireless communication systems, which may allow the wireless engineer to “customize” the uplink MIMO channels in the vicinity of BS by deploying a switchable FSS-based RIS in the proximity of the BS array.
the deployment of RIS to control massive MIMO channel characteristics in a way which is consistent with the underlying electromagnetic physics.
the development of a new electromagnetic paradigm for the deployment of reconfigurable surfaces to control the massive MIMO up-link channel’s eigenspectrum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the RIS can be deployed to control massive MIMO channel’s eigenvalue behaviour, and that such an electromagnetic framework may assist the wireless engineer to design the channel’s eigenvalue characteristics to suit the specific application.

the proposed RIS structure can be used to enhance the channel’s eigenvalue structure by selectively increasing the channel’s largest eigenvalue, or by selectively suppressing the channel’s smallest eigenvalue.

, in a wireless system where the channel’s eigenspectrum is a crucial parameter, an RIS based FSS structure can be utilized as a powerful tool to control the channel’s eigenvectors and eigenvalues, thereby assisting in the channel’s customization process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the RIS may be used as a powerful tool to control the channel characteristics, in a way that the wireless link engineer can “tune” the channel to a desirable behaviour, e.g. to enhance certain channel eigenvalues, to suppress certain eigenvalues, or to enhance the channel capacity, or to suppress the inter-user interference, and so forth.

the RIS may be utilized as an electromagnetic “toolkit” for the wireless link designer, who may use it to control the uplink channel’s eigenvalue structure, thereby enhancing the channel’s rank or suppressing its multipath richness.
RIS can be used as a “channel equalizer” to improve the uplink massive MIMO channel characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the RIS-based FSS can be used as a powerful tool to control the channel eigenvalues, which can be exploited by massive MIMO systems to improve the channel’s capacity, and by massive MIMO radar to improve the channel resolution and the target detection capability.
, by exploiting the RIS-based electromagnetic framework, the wireless engineer may now control the massive MIMO up/downlink channel characteristics in an unprecedented way.
the RIS can be used to “tune” the uplink massive MIMO channel’s eigensystem, thus enabling a more flexible and robust design of the uplink channel’s precoding matrix.
